digest.component_or_area: blocking link resolution and hierarchy escalation
propositions: The type-tier comparability rule produces silent edge misdirection: task T and story S both children of epic E cannot link directly; T depends_on S escalates to E depends_on S (epic blocked by its own child) and the requested edge is never written.
Cross-subtree dependencies should escalate to the nearest common ancestor's direct children, not by ticket type tier.
The redundancy guard is evaluated against the ORIGINAL endpoints before promotion, so promoted pairs that violate ancestor-descendant constraints (like epic-blocks-child) escape rejection.

Replacing type-tier with structural NCA-based comparability, re-evaluating redundancy from resolved endpoints only, and widening ancestor-walk cycle guards closes both bugs and prevents self-loops from being misclassified.

Blocking links whose resolved pair is ancestor-descendant (including direct parent-child and grandparent-grandchild) must be rejected as redundant; non-blocking relations keep the original-pair redundancy test unchanged.
